record.original_question: Given two distinct sets P1 and P2 of odd primes none of which is a subset of the other, is it true that ⟨CTP1(Z), CTP2(Z)⟩ ⪇ CTP1 ∪P2(Z)? See the definition of CTP(Z) in 17.60.

evidence.quote: Given two distinct sets P1 and P2 of odd primes none of which is a subset of the other, is it true that ⟨CTP1(Z), CTP2(Z)⟩ ⪇ CTP1 ∪P2(Z)? See the definition of CTP(Z) in 17.60.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Suppose that to every set $P$ of odd primes one associates a group $CT_P(\mathbb{Z})$ (the "$P$-congruence-transvection" group over $\mathbb{Z}$ as defined in the standard construction), with the property that $CT_{P}(\mathbb{Z}) \le CT_{Q}(\mathbb{Z})$ whenever $P \subseteq Q$. Let $P_1$ and $P_2$ be two distinct sets of odd primes such that neither is contained in the other, and inside the ambient group $CT_{P_1\cup P_2}(\mathbb{Z})$ form the subgroup $\langle CT_{P_1}(\mathbb{Z}),\, CT_{P_2}(\mathbb{Z})\rangle$ generated by $CT_{P_1}(\mathbb{Z})$ and $CT_{P_2}(\mathbb{Z})$. Decide whether one always has the strict inclusion
\[
\langle CT_{P_1}(\mathbb{Z}),\, CT_{P_2}(\mathbb{Z})\rangle \;\lneq\; CT_{P_1\cup P_2}(\mathbb{Z}).
\]
